status.en: 131 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 131 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen wounded former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami during a machete attack at his Abeokuta home, while security personnel continued to be targeted, with a university guard killed while returning home with his wife, another guard shot dead, and a herder shot dead in Plateau. Armed men also attacked a mining site in Plateau, leaving three feared dead. Rev. Ezekiel Dachomo mourned residents and a soldier killed in the latest Plateau attack. Police have launched a manhunt for the assailants of Odegbami and vowed to apprehend them. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenmenn såret den tidligere Super Eagles-kapteinen Segun Odegbami under et machetteangrep i hans hjem i Abeokuta, mens sikkerhetspersonell fortsatte å bli målrettet, med en universitetsvakt drept mens han kom hjem med sin kone, en annen vakt skutt død, og en hyrde skutt død i Plateau. Bevæpnede menn angrep også et gruveområde i Plateau, og tre personer fryktes drept. Rev. Ezekiel Dachomo sørget over innbyggere og en soldat drept i det siste angrepet i Plateau. Politiet har iverksatt en etterforskning av gjerningspersonene til Odegbami og lovet å pågripe dem. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
